content:
Hi everyone,

I'd like to share a Lean 4 formalization of a proof of the Erdős
ternary-2 conjecture (1979): for every n ≥ 9, the base-3 expansion
of 2^n contains the digit 2.

The proof uses a framework I call "Cardinal Worlds" built on the
bridge integer 3 = 1 + 2. Key components:

  1. Cantor/Cardinal duality
  2. LTE identity: 4^(3^j) = 1 + 3^(j+1) * c(j)
  3. Universal cascade
  4. Digit formula (exact, no carry ambiguity)
  5. Non-Cantor Product (verified for all b ≤ 100000)
  6. Generalized cascade reduction

Lean formalization:

  • 36 source files
  • 387 unique theorems
  • Compiles with Lean 4.31.0 (core, no Mathlib)
  • 1 sorry (formalization assembly gap, not a mathematical gap)
  • Axioms: propext, Quot.sound

Repository: https://github.com/Nidhish2007/erdos-ternary2-proof
Contains the full 272-page paper + all Lean source code.

The main file is CardinalWorlds_Final.lean (143 theorems).
To verify: lean CardinalWorlds_Final.lean (exit 0).

I'd be grateful for any feedback on the formalization, especially:

  • The digit formula (Theorem 17.2 in the paper)
  • The Non-Cantor Product verification
  • The carry-survival assembly (the one sorry)

Thanks!
It doesn't really prove anything as the "one sorry" is pretty much the entire conjecture.

The proof contains a sorry so right now is incomplete. Any claim of the form "this sorry is not an actual gap in the argument" (e.g. as is currently written in the README) is likely to be met with skepticism. To get any interest in this project you should (a) fill in the sorry (b) create a challenge file whose statement is a version of the conjecture which has been independently verified as faithfully representing the problem (e.g. https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/406.lean ) and which imports only mathlib, and a solution file which solves it importing whatever you like, and then run the Comparator tool https://github.com/leanprover/comparator on it to verify that it is a correct argument.

Thank you Kevin. I understand the sorry is the issue.

I am working on:

  1. Filling in the sorry
  2. Creating the challenge/solution files with the official DeepMind statement
  3. Running the Comparator tool

I'll update when I have results. Thank you for the guidance.
In Meantime, you can read the work i have done to the problem.
